articles.title: New Knicks Rumors on Roster Plans After Drew Eubanks' Pectoral Injury Ahead of NBA Season Opener
articles.summary: The New York Knicks will be forced to pivot after losing veteran center Drew Eubanks to a torn pectoral injury.
articles.body:
The New York Knicks will be forced to pivot after losing veteran center Drew Eubanks to a torn pectoral injury.

ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Knicks are expected to waive Eubanks, who had been competing for a roster spot. Kristian Winfield noted that Eubanks' absence left James Wiseman and Tony Bradley competing for New York's third-string center position, with Wiseman considered "the favorite."

Bradley was subsequently waived later on Thursday.

ESPN's Bobby Marks noted that the Knicks will have a salary cap hit of just $15,000 because Eubanks was signed to an Exhibit 9 contract. Without it, the team would have been responsible for his salary during his recovery process.

Eubanks had played in three out of New York's four preseason games, most recently producing eight points, two rebounds, two assists and a block in 15 minutes off the bench in Tuesday's loss to the Toronto Raptors.

A nine-year veteran, Eubanks appeared to be the frontrunner for the Knicks' third center spot thanks to his experience. He spent the 2025-26 campaign with the Sacramento Kings, and he previously played for the Los Angeles Clippers, Utah Jazz, Phoenix Suns, Portland Trail Blazers and San Antonio Spurs.

As Winfield noted, Eubanks' injury opens the door for Wiseman, the 2020 No. 2 pick who is trying to avoid being labeled as a draft bust. In Tuesday's game against Toronto, Wiseman led New York with 18 points on 7-of-8 shooting and 10 rebounds.

The Knicks need depth behind Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond, so another strong performance for Wiseman in Thursday night's rematch against the Raptors could be enough for him to secure a roster spot.

articles.title: Jeremy Lin, Jason Kidd Join ESPN as NBA Analysts Ahead of 2026 Season
articles.summary: Former NBA guard Jeremy Lin is one of the latest athletes to try his hand at broadcasting.
articles.body:
Former NBA guard Jeremy Lin is one of the latest athletes to try his hand at broadcasting.

ESPN announced on Thursday that Lin has been hired as a contributor to NBA Today and a game analyst for the 2026-27 NBA season.

In addition to Lin's arrival, ESPN also hired former floor general and head coach Jason Kidd, who was fired by the Dallas Mavericks earlier this offseason. The Hall of Famer will be a member of the new NBA Countdown lineup, and he will serve as a game analyst throughout the year.

ESPN already boasts a long list of former players and coaches who have found success in their second careers as broadcasters, including Kendrick Perkins, Richard Jefferson, Tim Legler, Iman Shumpert, Danny Green, P.J. Carlesimo and more.

Kidd and Lin will bring new insight as former point guards who know what it takes to make it in the NBA, so fans should be excited to see their foray into broadcasting.

articles.title: Aliyah Boston Injury Update, Timeline to Return to Fever After Knee Surgery to Repair Meniscus
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever announced Thursday that star forward Aliyah Boston underwent surgery to repair her right meniscus.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever announced Thursday that star forward Aliyah Boston underwent surgery to repair her right meniscus.

The team didn't provide a timeframe for her recovery as it relates to the 2027 WNBA season.

Boston averaged 16.1 points and 8.0 rebounds this season, earning her fourth All-Star selection. She battled leg trouble throughout the year , though it didn't seem to impact her in the playoffs. She averaged 19.7 points on 58.1 percent shooting, including 45.5 percent on threes, in the first round against the Las Vegas Aces.

Trade Ideas for Eliminated Playoff Teams💡

Even assuming she's on the court for opening night, Boston's surgery is another offseason variable for the Fever when they already have a lot on their plate.

Four-time All-Star Kelsey Mitchell is an unrestricted free agent, and she indicated she plans to at least explore all of her options. Three-point specialist Sophie Cunningham is headed for the open market as well.

Even if Indiana runs it back, the team probably can't count on continued improvement from Caitlin Clark as the one thing that will propel it to the 2027 Finals.

The trouble is, there aren't a lot of marquee names hitting free agency , and two of the biggest on the board, Napheesa Collier and Jackie Young, may not leave their current teams.

This is going to be a consequential and tricky offseason for the Fever as they try to build a championship-caliber roster around Clark and Boston. Knee surgery for the latter doesn't help matters.

articles.title: NBA GMs Pick MVP, Champion, ROY, Top Offseason Moves, More in Annual Survey
articles.summary: Twenty-three of 30 NBA general managers believe that San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama will win his first-ever NBA MVP award this upcoming season.
articles.body:
Twenty-three of 30 NBA general managers believe that San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama will win his first-ever NBA MVP award this upcoming season.

Those results were revealed in the 25th and latest edition of the Annual NBA GM Survey , which dropped Thursday courtesy of NBA.com's John Schuhmann.

General managers answered 48 questions in the survey. Here's a look at answers from some of the most notable questions, including MVP, champion, rookie of the year, top offseason moves and more.

1. San Antonio Spurs C Victor Wembanyama, San Antonio (23 votes)

2. Denver Nuggets C Nikola Jokić (3 votes)

3. Minnesota Timberwolves SG Anthony Edwards (2 votes)

4. Oklahoma City Thunder PG Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Boston Celtics F Jayson Tatum (1 vote each)

1. Memphis Grizzlies F Cameron Boozer (15 votes)

2. Chicago Bulls F Caleb Wilson (6 votes)

3. Washington Wizards F AJ Dybantsa (5 votes)

4. Boston Celtics, Minnesota Timberwolves, Toronto Raptors (1 vote each)

Other questions included biggest draft steal (Milwaukee Bucks guard Brayden Burries, 10 votes), best head coach (Miami Heat's Erik Spoelstra, 13 votes), most fun team to watch (Minnesota Timberwolves and San Antonio Spurs, nine votes each) and most improved team (Indiana Pacers, 13 votes).

Regarding MVP, it's no surprise Wembanyama is leading the way, even if Oklahoma City Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is the back-to-back award winner. The 22-year-old is an ascending superstar who just averaged 25.0 points, 11.5 rebounds and an NBA-high 3.1 blocks in his third season en route to leading the 62-win Spurs to a Western Conference title.

The Spurs have the slight edge on the Thunder for the championship, but it's clear those two are far-and-away the top contenders on paper. Oklahoma City won 64 games last year and cruised to the Western Conference Finals after back-to-back sweeps, but they fell in seven to the Spurs. Both teams returned their talents and added some more in hopes of securing the Larry O'Brien Trophy.

Rookie of the Year looks to be a heated race. Memphis Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer and Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson are going to get many chances to star and be featured for their young, rebuilding teams and could vault themselves up the ROY race because of them.

As for top offseason moves, it's no surprise the Philadelphia 76ers are No. 1 after adding Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, forming one of the NBA's best starting lineups. The 76ers should be a strong Eastern Conference contender and arguably stand as the Knicks' biggest threat to back-to-back titles.

The NBA season begins on Tuesday with a triple-header headlined by the Knicks hosting James and the 76ers.

articles.title: Fever star Aliyah Boston undergoes right knee surgery following team's playoff loss to Aces
articles.summary: Aliyah Boston turned in fantastic numbers in 2026.
articles.body:
By all accounts, Indiana Fever star Aliyah Boston turned in yet another fantastic season in 2026. The 24-year-old averaged a career-high 16.1 points per game and made the All-Star team for the fourth straight year.

She was equally fantastic in the playoffs, averaging 19.6 points in a three-game series loss against the Las Vegas Aces.

Boston apparently managed some of that excellence despite an ailing right knee. With the Fever's 2026 season over, Boston underwent surgery to repair her meniscus Wednesday, the team announced.

The Fever did not announce a timeline for Boston's return, saying it would provide further updates "as they become available."

It's unclear exactly when Boston sustained the injury, though she was forced to leave a game in late July after a hard fall. Boston clutched her right knee after the play, causing plenty of concern among Fever fans.

Despite that, Boston was able to return and play in the team's next game, dropping 14 points in a win over the Portland Fire.

Since being drafted No. 1 overall by the Fever in 2023, Boston has emerged as one of the best players in the WNBA. After winning the Rookie of the Year award in her first season, Boston turned in an All-Star season in her second year before getting MVP consideration in her third season.

The Fever have steadily improved in each of Boston's first four seasons. After finishing with one of the worst records in the WNBA during Boston's first season, the Fever went 28-16 in 2026.

As long as Boston is fully recovered by the start of next season, the Fever should have a shot at improving and contending for a championship in 2027.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards Sends NSFW Warning to NBA in Video Ahead of LaMelo Ball's Debut T-Wolves Season
articles.summary: Anthony Edwards has a message for the rest of the NBA.
articles.body:
Anthony Edwards has a message for the rest of the NBA.

The Minnesota Timberwolves star let the rest of the league know how his new team plans on approaching the 2026-27 campaign in a NSFW video on his YouTube page .

"When y'all see the Timberwolves come to town … they on bulls--t," he said. "We gonna foul the s--t out of you. … Yeah, we on that. I just want you all to know, that's what's going on. … Get your season tickets because s--t's going to be turned up this year. If you miss a game, you're going to miss out."

Minnesota has been to the Western Conference Finals in two of the last three years but is yet to get over the hump and reach the NBA Finals with Edwards leading the way.

But it is going to look quite different in 2026-27 with the addition of LaMelo Ball in particular, as well as Jonathan Kuminga on the wing. Naz Reid and Julius Randle are also gone, meaning there may be even more scoring responsibility on Edwards' shoulders.

Having Ball could help him with that, as the point guard is a capable distributor and can create matchup problems by forcing defenses to extend to deal with his three-point shooting. He is also capable of taking over stretches of games as a scorer and could have even better looks on the outside when Edwards is doubled.

It seems like the Timberwolves are also going to have a physical style of play if Edwards' comments are any indication, which could wear on opponents over the course of a long playoff series.

He is encouraging fans to get their season tickets, and they will have the first chance to see what it looks like on Oct. 21 when Ball makes his Minnesota debut in the season opener against the Miami Heat.

articles.title: New Karl-Anthony Towns Rumors Reveal Potential NBA Landing Spots Amid Knicks Contract Dispute
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Clippers stand out as the top two potential suitors for New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns if he leaves the team via free agency next offseason, an anonymous NBA executive told Stefan Bondy of the New York Post.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls and Los Angeles Clippers stand out as the top two potential suitors for New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns if he leaves the team via free agency next offseason, an anonymous NBA executive told Stefan Bondy of the New York Post .

"Only a few possible suitors stand out to me right now in terms of cap space teams and fit. Chicago and the Clippers have the cleanest path," the executive said. "The Nets can get there with the money, but that's not a good fit. Golden State and Dallas could get around [$50 million] in space with more tinkering."

Towns has a $61 million player option for next season, but according to ESPN's Bobby Marks " the player option must be eliminated and replaced with the first year of the extension" if he signs after that date.

The Knicks previously offered Towns a four-year, $200 million contract extension, per ESPN's Shams Charania . He is eligible for a $276 million extension.

On Friday, Oct. 9, the Knicks announced that they are tabling all contract extension discussions (guards Josh Hart, Miles McBride and Tyler Kolek are also eligible).

"As an organization, our entire focus is preparing for the upcoming season and delivering another year for our fans to be proud of," a statement read. "As a result, we will not be negotiating contract extensions until later in the season and will remain solely focused on preparing for the start of the season."

Towns issued remarks after the team's Oct. 11 practice.

"It was news to me," Towns told reporters . "Very disappointed to say the least. Let's state the obvious: It's business, but there is business on the court for us to handle."

For now, that business starts on Tuesday, when the Knicks begin their NBA title defense against the Philadelphia 76ers at home.

articles.title: Steph Curry Addresses Warriors' LeBron James Pursuit, 'Happy' for 76ers Star After NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: There was plenty of buzz about the Golden State Warriors potentially pursuing LeBron James this offseason, but Stephen Curry is still "happy" for his friend after the King chose the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
There was plenty of buzz about the Golden State Warriors potentially pursuing LeBron James this offseason, but Stephen Curry is still "happy" for his friend after the King chose the Philadelphia 76ers.

But he also told SiriusXM NBA Radio he thought there was a "conversation" to be had about teaming up with his fellow legend.

"If there was ever some momentum it would be known, based on the profile that LeBron has, if he picks up the phone and says, 'Hey, what's going on out there,' or vice versa and I pick up the phone and say, 'Hey, what's on your mind,'" Curry said. "You want to be in the conversation for a guy like that who is picking his landing spot."

"... As a friend and an Olympic teammate, I'm happy for him that he found somewhere he wants to be."

The idea of James and Curry playing together is one plenty of NBA fans have thought about for years. After all, they defined a generation of the league together with a combined eight championships and six MVPs as two of the greatest players in the sport's history.

They have also seemed like such a perfect pairing for so long as well considering Curry's gravitational pull as an outside shooter creates so much driving space for someone like James to attack the rim.

Throw in their combined basketball IQs and ability to make the play seemingly every time they have the ball in their hands, and it would have been appointment viewing.

But it seems like the only time fans will see them play on the same team is in the Olympics after James decided to join the 76ers this offseason.

It's certainly hard to blame the future Hall of Famer, as the combination of James, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid should put Philadelphia on the short list of realistic championship contenders if they can all stay healthy.

As for Curry, he will look to help the Warriors bounce back after they were eliminated in the play-in tournament last season.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Explains Why Taking Year Off from NBA Was 'Best Thing I've Done In My Career'
articles.summary: After a year away from the NBA, a rejuvenated Ben Simmons is looking to revive his career with the Sacramento Kings.
articles.body:
After a year away from the NBA, a rejuvenated Ben Simmons is looking to revive his career with the Sacramento Kings.

Simmons spoke to NBC Sports California's Deuce Mason and Morgan Ragan about why his year off was necessary following a lengthy run of injuries.

"I just think for myself, I needed it. People can say what they want about not wanting to play, this, that and the third. But I needed to get away from the game, I needed to get my back right to be able to play this game at a high level," Simmons said (1:08 mark). "I think the one thing people kept saying to me was, 'It's gonna be hard to get back.' And I was fine with that, but I also know what I'm able to give the game. So taking that year off is the best thing I've done in my career."

Simmons was once one of the brightest young stars in the NBA, but he endured some difficult setbacks that caused him to lose his mojo.

The 30-year-old showed some signs of his old self in his lone preseason appearance for the Kings, scoring seven points in nine minutes against the Golden State Warriors last Saturday.

If Simmons can return to form as a reliable two-way contributor, he could help the Kings accelerate their rebuild as they try to keep pace in the talented Western Conference.

articles.title: Where Caleb Wilson ranks on top NBA player lists ahead of much anticipate rookie season
articles.summary: The Chicago Bulls aren’t necessarily putting all their eggs in the Caleb Wilson basket. That being said, there is no question that Wilson will have all eyes...
articles.body:
The Chicago Bulls aren't necessarily putting all their eggs in the Caleb Wilson basket. That being said, there is no question that Wilson will have all eyes on him .

With the NBA season beginning next week, various outlets have released their Top 100 NBA player lists. Wilson has made some of those lists .

On Wednesday, Bleacher Report ranked Wilson No. 99. In September, ESPN ranked Wilson No. 97 in its system. CBS Sports officially ranked Wilson No. 4 in their Top 10 NBA rookies.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

That being said, The Ringer's Top 100 player list didn't include Wilson. They instead included his teammates Josh Giddey, Matas Buzelis, and Norman Powell.

However, there is no denying Wilson's potential going into his debut season. Some are expecting Wilson to be a Rookie of the Year candidate .

In June, Wilson was the No.4 pick in the NBA Draft . He arrives in Chicago from the University of North Carolina with a playing style that mirrors what new executive Bryson Graham calls his SLAP acronym (size, length, athleticism, and physicality).

Wilson is all that in one player. He provides a unique combination of strength, agility, leadership, and poise that goes well beyond his young years.

In the Summer League in July, Wilson had an award-winning stint . He averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals, and 2.5 blocks while making the All-Summer League First Team.

The Bulls are looking to begin a new era with a new approach after years of the same old, same old. As a result, they are banking in part on Wilson living up to his potential.

So far, Wilson has had a solid preseason. He is averaging 15.8 points, 3.8 rebounds, and 2.3 assists per game.

articles.title: 2026-27 Fantasy Basketball Draft Strategy Mega Guide
articles.summary: Rotoworld's fantasy basketball experts reveal their favorite picks and players to avoid in each of the first 10 rounds, plus their preferred draft strategies...
articles.body:
Whether you're a fantasy basketball veteran or a novice, everyone can use a little help with the draft process.

With that in mind, the Rotoworld Fantasy Basketball crew has put together a mega guide packed with the players we're targeting, the ones we're avoiding, and the potential values worth watching ahead of the 2026-27 season.

Be sure to have this link handy during your upcoming drafts, as well as Rotoworld's FREE 2026-27 Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit! Download it here !

Your one-stop-shop for all of Rotoworld's preseason content leading into fantasy basketball drafts.

▶ Who is your favorite pick in each round?

Count me among those who believe this season will be the start of the "Wemby Era" regarding the best player in fantasy basketball. He may not offer assists at the level that Nikola Jokić does, but good luck finding a skilled big capable of throwing up a triple-double (with blocks) on any given night. And don't be surprised if Wembanyama has a game in which he approaches a quadruple-double. - Raphielle Johnson

Everyone will remember just how good Giannis is this year. I'm not sure exactly how good the Heat will be, but Giannis will be a star. Perhaps it's best to punt free-throw percentage, but he's good enough to make it worth it. - Noah Rubin

He's always in the running to be fantasy's top overall player, and he's been surprisingly durable throughout his career. Win-win. - Zak Hanshew

Getting Towns in the second round of any draft would be a steal. The 7-footer provided top-25 value last season, and the Knicks did not look to feature KAT more offensively until the playoffs. That shift sparked a 13-game win streak and helped the Knicks win their first NBA title since 1973. While Jalen Brunson is now healthy, he's coming off left wrist surgery, which is another reason to expect more of the offense to run through KAT, especially early on. - RJ

I get the hesitancy with him coming off an Achilles tear, but Haliburton is a fantasy star. He may get back to leading the league in assists immediately, and he has a squad ready to bounce back after a tumultuous season. - NR

Curry's ADP is the second-to-last pick in the second round of fantasy drafts, but he's finished in the Top 10 in 15 of 17 seasons. That's the definition of upside, baby! - ZH

Productivity has never been an issue for Leonard; availability has. He's back in Toronto and has the contract extension he desired, which should help the three-time NBA champion hit the ground running. Beyond the offense, sharing the court with Scottie Barnes could help Leonard defensively and raise his fantasy ceiling. - RJ

Leonard has finished inside the Top 10 in eight of the last 11 seasons, and he finished no worse than 33rd in 8-cat formats in each of the last 12 seasons. He can easily outperform his current ADP. - ZH

An injury-riddled season on a tanking team made us forget how good Sabonis is. He's a potential first-rounder who stuffs the stat sheet. Sacramento's offense should run through him, and he'll be one of the league's best rebounders again. - NR

White may not be the most prolific option for fantasy managers, but he has been reliable over the years. Despite shooting a career-low 39.4 percent from the field last season, the Celtics guard provided third-round value in nine-cat formats. Like Tatum, White could benefit from Jaylen Brown's exit, even with Paul George in the fold. - RJ

G/F Jalen Williams, Oklahoma City Thunder

Frankly, I'd take JDub as early as round two. He's healthy now! Williams has been a fantasy star throughout his career, and he should get back to that this season. - NR

Injury risk is baked into his draft-day price, but AD has first-round upside in spades. - ZH

Jackson only played three games for the Jazz after he was acquired from the Grizzlies, but his performance in those outings was promising. Plus, with Jusuf Nurkić in the fold, JJJ should be able to play his preferred power forward position instead of slotting in at center. For most of his career, playing alongside a physical center has benefited Jackson, especially defensively. I think getting him in the fifth round represents good value. - RJ

The Jazz have the roster to allow Jackson to thrive. He isn't being asked to lead the team in scoring, and he isn't being asked to dominate the glass. He can return to being one of the league's best shot blockers while still contributing elsewhere. - NR

Boozer is the new face of the franchise, and he's got a fantasy-friendly two-way skill set that should help pay off his mid-round asking price. - ZH

As was the case last season, Anunoby feels undervalued in fantasy basketball circles. To get a player of his caliber this late in a draft would be a steal. He was close to a top-25 player in category leagues, and like Towns, OG stands to benefit if the Knicks decide to spread the playmaking workload more evenly, as they did to great effect in the spring. - RJ

The toe is healed! Garland is running the show for the first time since before the Cavaliers traded for Donovan Mitchell. There have been a few rough years, but it's time for Garland to shine. - NR

Herro could legitimately lead the NBA in scoring if he stays healthy. The Bucks are in full rebuild after trading away Giannis Antetokounmpo, and Herro should see plenty of usage and a ton of shots. - ZH

Last season wasn't great for Bridges in fantasy basketball. However, availability won't be an issue for a player who hasn't missed a game in his NBA career. Bridges' fantasy ceiling may not be particularly high, but I like his floor. - RJ

I think I'm buying in on PG in Boston. I'm even more bought in at this price. Health is always a concern, but he should still supply steals, and the Celtics should shoot a ton of threes, which should work well for George. - NR

Wilson can be Chicago's go-to offensive option, but he's also an effective defender who can fill out the stat sheet across multiple categories. - ZH

It's a new era in Memphis, and the expectation is that Coward will be one of the leaders. He has the offensive skill set to be a major asset to fantasy managers, especially in category leagues. I'm betting on Coward to be close to a top-50 player this season. - RJ

With Nic Claxton in Chicago, the starting center spot in Brooklyn officially belongs to Sharpe. He has been dominant in limited action over the last few years, and he should be in for a breakout season. Expect him to be dominant on the glass and have success as a playmaker. - NR

There is a ton of risk in taking a guy who just got traded and has played so few games in recent seasons. This late in the draft, however, I'm willing to take a swing on an upside talent like Morant. - ZH

Limited to 33 games in his first full season with the Raptors, Quickley made 70 appearances last season and was close to a top-50 player. While adding Kawhi Leonard could cut into his usage, Quickley is a good enough shooter to provide excellent value as a three-point threat. Ninth-round value is way too low for him. - RJ

I'm apparently going to draft a lot of Kings. Similar to Sabonis, LaVine had an injury-riddled year on a tanking team. But he's way too good to go outside the top-100. It feels safe to say he'll outplay this ADP. - NR

Last season was rough for LaVine and Sac-Town, and injuries hampered his overall production. If he can stay healthy, LaVine should far outpace his current ADP, as he's been an early-to-mid-round guy throughout his career. - ZH

I've had my doubts about Jerome in the past, but he's in a very good position going into the 2026-27 campaign. First, he's healthy after injuries limited him to 15 games last season. Also, Ja Morant was traded to Portland. Someone has to get the ball to guys like Zach Edey, Cedric Coward, and Cameron Boozer and Jerome is the Grizzlies point guard best equipped to do it. - RJ

F/C Collin Murray-Boyles, Toronto Raptors

I'm really excited to see how Toronto uses CMB this season. Perhaps not for long stretches, but I think lineups with Scottie Barnes and CMB at power forward and center could be intriguing. We're in upside-swing territory, and CMB could be a fantasy superstar with enough chances. - NR

Robinson will no longer be lurking in the shadows as a backup, and he should be the top option in Boston's frontcourt. He's a per-minute monster who's about to see plenty more playing time. - ZH

▶ Who is your least favorite pick in each round?

Antetokounmpo will begin a new chapter in his NBA career when he suits up for the Heat, with the franchise expecting to be contenders in the East. Fantasy-wise, while he certainly has his strengths, I'm not too keen on using a first-round pick on a player who can put you in a position where you're punting multiple categories. - RJ

I think there's a scenario where Johnson improves this season, but it won't translate to fantasy basketball. He was rough down the stretch last season after they traded for CJ McCollum, but I expect they'll figure that out this summer. His efficiency should return, but he'll have the ball in his hands less. The defense also slipped last season, though I'm hoping he can focus on that end more this year. He still has the ceiling of a first-rounder, but I'm afraid he has the lowest floor of every player with a first-round ADP. - NR

I just can't see a realistic pathway to first-round value with Jaylen Brown, LeBron James and an improved bench around him. - ZH

I get it. With LeBron James gone, Reaves steps up to be the Lakers' second option behind Luka Dončić. That said, selecting him in the second round of standard drafts feels like a reach. Better options are likely on the board; Reaves is a better choice in the third round of 12-team drafts. - RJ

This has nothing to do with Brunson's talent. This has everything to do with how they'll use him. If they want to repeat, they'll have to manage Brunson's usage and minutes this upcoming season. The points, assists and threes are valuable, but he doesn't excel in other categories. Now, his minutes could drop, which would mean less of everything. I'm way more interested in taking him in round three or four. - NR

He's a mid-round guy, but I'm not taking him in the Top 24. Şengün doesn't rack up enough defensive stats for a big man, and his field-goal percentage is far from elite. His free-throw percentage is dreadful, and he doesn't shoot threes. Where's the second-round upside? - ZH

Selecting Brown in the third round of a standard draft means you're expecting him to threaten top-25 status in fantasy value. That's something he never did in Boston, even last season with Jayson Tatum recovering from a ruptured Achilles. Are we expecting Brown to do that in Philadelphia with that loaded starting lineup? I don't see it. - RJ

Brown is coming off posting career-best averages in points, rebounds and assists, and he still arguably wasn't worth a third-round pick. Now, he certainly isn't. This team has too much talent for all of them to thrive in the box score. - NR

I was out on Duren this early in drafts before his messy contract negotiations, and he's now on my "Do Not Draft" list. This is a ridiculously high asking price for a guy who disappeared in the playoffs and now has to compete with John Collins for frontcourt minutes. - ZH

By the grace of the basketball gods, I finished second in a league in which I selected Davis in the second round (and Walker Kessler in the third). The fourth round feels like a much better place to select AD, but his injury history makes him untrustworthy in fantasy basketball. Let someone else take that risk. - RJ

I was lower on Knueppel before, but with him set to miss the preseason with a hamstring injury, I don't see how anyone can take him this early. I'm concerned he won't repeat his rookie success without LaMelo Ball, especially with teams having a more robust scouting report, and the hamstring injury terrifies me. - NR

Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice… You know the rest. He burned me last year with a lukewarm showing, and the Pacers will have Tyrese Haliburton and Ivica Zubac back. No thanks. - ZH

Castle is a player whose "real" value far outweighs his fantasy value, especially in category leagues. He'll play plenty, but managers should not use a fifth-round pick on Castle, even if they are betting on his upside. - RJ

I like Castle as a player, but I don't think there's much fantasy appeal here. Certainly not this much. His main fantasy appeal is his assists, but Dylan Harper's emergence could eat into that. The percentages are rough, and he's not a high-volume scorer. I just think taking him here eliminates any upside. - NR

Castle had another productive season, but he finished outside the Top 150 in per-game fantasy value because of inefficient shooting, a lack of three-pointers and modest scoring. His situation has not improved enough to warrant a Top-60 pick. - ZH

This pick has little to do with Herro's skill level and everything to do with the Bucks' crowded backcourt. Kevin Porter Jr. and Gary Trent Jr. were re-signed, Ryan Rollins and AJ Green are also back, and Milwaukee used one of its lottery picks on Brayden Burries. Herro, who's going into a contract year, will clearly be motivated to put up big numbers. But this isn't the best situation for him in terms of fantasy potential. - RJ

G Damian Lillard, Portland Trail Blazers

I just can't confidently take a 36-year-old coming off an Achilles tear this early, especially when he's sharing minutes with Ja Morant, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. This feels too early for such a risky pick, even when it's a player as accomplished as Dame. - NR

His breakout is over, as the Wiz completely retooled their lineup with Anthony Davis, Deandre Ayton, AJ Dybantsa and Trae Young. Expect a drop in counting stats and a finish outside the sixth round. - ZH

Given his defensive issues, I have a hard time believing Queen will be the starting center ahead of Yves Missi if the Pelicans go with a traditional five. They could also go with Zion Williamson at that position, and the tandem of him and Queen was abysmal defensively last season. Queen's long-term outlook is good, especially if the Pelicans clean up that roster, but the short term isn't great for fantasy basketball. - RJ

I like Queen as a prospect for the future, but is everyone aware he may not start this season? Last year, Queen and Zion Williamson didn't work well together on the floor. It didn't work offensively, and it was even worse defensively. I wouldn't take Queen anywhere near the seventh round.

Rollins was a great early-season star, but the Bucks added Tyler Herro, drafted Brayden Burries and brought back Kevin Porter Jr. There's no clear pathway to a Round 7 fantasy finish. - ZH

Sharpe is coming off the most productive season of his NBA career, posting new highs in points, rebounds, assists and steals. However, to expect him to suddenly become a top-100 player feels a bit much, even with Nic Claxton now in Chicago. - RJ

After the Spurs' run, it seems everyone is writing De'Aaron Fox out of the equation. Like the Spurs are going to bench him and play him 18 minutes per game. He's still the starter! Harper will play a significant role off the bench, but this isn't the year he becomes a fantasy star. Plus, Castle is still there too, and he's the one who will have the ball in his hands. - NR

Harper had a tremendous rookie campaign that culminated in a strong showing in the NBA Finals. Still, it will be tough to carry that momentum into big-time fantasy play with De'Aaron Fox and Stephon Castle still ahead of him on the depth chart. - ZH

Given where Turner was picked in drafts before last season, the ninth round is far more realistic. However, we're talking about a player whose rebounding woes reached a point where he lost out on minutes to Jericho Sims. With the Bucks adding Kel'el Ware as part of the Giannis trade, Turner's hold on the starting center role may be shaky, even with his hefty contract. - RJ

I get it. The opportunity that Jaquez and other players on this team will have is enticing. However, that doesn't mean it will translate to fantasy production. There's more appeal in points leagues or in specific category league builds, but is he even locked in as a starter?

JSJ is a poor shooter who doesn't pile up defensive stats and doesn't rebound at a high level. I'm not excited to draft him at his ceiling here. - ZH

People know the Jazz are going to look to compete this season, right? Filipowski certainly has talent, but envisioning a scenario in which he's a must-draft player is extremely challenging. - RJ

I'm still a believer in Fears. However, he's still so young and is on a team that's probably going to struggle again. Plus, he likely won't start. We'll try again next year, hopefully after they've made some moves. - NR

This team is too deep to consider Simons anything more than a three-point specialist. Higher-upside options are available at this point in the draft. - ZH

Brandon Miller has a chance to shine in Charlotte, while Dylan Harper is among several young players looking to make a leap in 2026-27.

▶ What is your favorite punt build, and why?

Turnovers may be the easiest category to punt, because your available options include the most ball-dominant players in the game. Luka Dončić remains one of the best options in fantasy basketball with this approach, which also raises the ceilings of guards like Stephen Curry and Trae Young.

You can always punt just one percentage, which lets you maximize certain players considered a liability in that category. However, punting both works even better. It's not about finding players that struggle at both, but about not worrying when players miss shots. Plus, players are far more likely to have a hot shooting night than to luck into extra assists. I'll enjoy the shot-chuckers and Hack-a-Shaq candidates who contribute in multiple ways. - NR

Aside from SGA, the league's best guards aren't the most efficient shooters, and punting this category improves their value significantly. Tyrese Maxey, Luka Doncic, Stephen Curry and James Harden are all strong options for this build. - ZH

▶ What is your least favorite punt build, and why?

Guards tend to dominate the top of the fantasy rankings, and you'll see the assist category in just about every league. So why punt it? Ceding this category comes with significant risk, as many of the players most proficient in assists also offer excellent value in other areas. - RJ

It's about what I enjoy, right? It's a fine strategy if you execute it, but it can be incredibly risky. Points are one of the more consistent categories, and I prefer to know what I'm getting from as many categories as possible. Plus, I just don't have as much fun! - NR

This build can get a little confusing early in drafts, since all of the first-round and most second-round options are prolific scorers. This build focuses on later rounds, when you can find value in peripheral-category players rather than elite offensive options. Getting this one right can be tricky, and I prefer to stay away. - ZH

You can address positional needs via trade or the waiver wire after the draft ends. In the moment, take the best player available. And if you land the right player, another manager's need could boost your asking price. - RJ

Every single team. Don't take a lesser player for positional need. Make trades later to fill out your roster before the playoffs, but maximize the pieces you have early on. - NR

My favorite exercise is ranking my Top-200 blindly and then comparing it to ADP. When I rank a player higher than ADP, I consider him a value; vice versa if I rank him lower. I also look at a player's fantasy history, injury risk and how their situation has changed heading into the new season to gauge their range of outcomes and peg them as a safe or risky option. - ZH

▶ How do you leverage rankings to your advantage while drafting?

Making sure I understand the connection between the rankings and the rules of the league I'm playing in. Just because a player is high in the default rankings doesn't make them a great fit for your particular league. I also want to make sure I have a solid grasp of the player's situation regarding their team's depth chart. Don't reach for someone who isn't guaranteed to play significant rotation minutes. - RJ

Rankings help me decide when it's worth taking players. If it's a player I'm high on, I'll go earlier than their ranking. If it's a player I'm low on, their ranking helps me decide whether I'm fine with taking them after their ADP. - NR

Rankings vary from platform to platform, so know where you're playing and review the rankings before your draft to spot glaring outliers. Make sure you understand your leaguemates' tendencies. Are you drafting with a bunch of sharps, or are you playing with guys who rely solely on the consensus rankings without paying too much attention to the NBA? Know where you're playing and who you're playing with, and you can leverage rankings to your advantage every time. - ZH

▶ How soon do you reach for your "guys"? Describe your approach to reaching in general.

In snake drafts, I'll consider reaching from the fourth round onward. The first three rounds are where I seek "cornerstones," guys who I'm going to rely on to have a major impact, barring injury. - RJ

After I fill out my starters, I'll reach for anyone. You don't win your league by playing safe. Get the guys you know will be good that still have upside, and then start swinging for the fences. If it doesn't work out, drop them and stream. - NR

I don't like to play it safe in drafts - never have and never will. Fantasy basketball is about having fun, and what better way to have fun than to get your favorite players on your team… within reason. I'm a LeBron fan through and through, but I won't be taking him in the second round. If he's available in the fourth round or later, however, I'm all in. I'm not reaching in the first three rounds, but after that, all bets are off, and I'll happily reach 10-15 spots early to go and get my guys, especially if I don't think they'll make it back to me. - ZH

▶ Name three players you're much higher on than the consensus.

Raphielle: F OG Anunoby (New York Knicks), G/F Cedric Coward (Memphis Grizzlies) and G Immanuel Quickley (Toronto Raptors)

As noted above, I'm extremely high on Anunoby. While there were availability concerns in the past, he's played 74 and 67 games in his two full seasons with the Knicks. Given the energy a team spends pursuing a championship, the Knicks will likely have to spread the wealth more this season, which should benefit Anunoby.

Coward is in an excellent spot in Memphis as the franchise rebuilds. He took on a leadership role during Summer League and that will remain the case in the wing's second season. As long as Coward stays healthy, we should see the skill set that made him a lottery pick last summer.

Quickley boasts top-50 fantasy potential, even with Kawhi Leonard returning to Toronto. I'm all-in on him this season as the Raptors become a factor in the East.

Noah: G/F Jalen Williams (Oklahoma City Thunder), G Darius Garland (LA Clippers), and G/F Zach LaVine (Sacramento Kings)

Again, I think last season really impacted how people view JDub. I'm expecting him to be a top-25 player this season. That may mean it's best to get him closer to his ADP to maximize value, but Williams will bounce back in a big way. - NR

Garland was really good down the stretch for the Clippers, and after spending multiple seasons next to Donovan Mitchell, he'll have his own squad to run. Brandon Ingram is the other ball-dominant star on the team, but Garland will get the ball more and should be in for his best statistical season yet.

LaVine should be back to offensive star status. The Kings will try to be competitive, which means LaVine should have the ball in his hands plenty. I don't view him as a late-round target, but as a middle-round option with upside to be more.

Zak: F Yaxel Lendeborg (Golden State Warriors), C Mitchell Robinson (Boston Celtics) and G Coby White (Charlotte Hornets)

The No. 11 overall pick led the Dubs to a Summer League title with strong, across-the-board production. With Jimmy Butler likely sidelined to open the 2026-27 season, Lendeborg has a path to immediate minutes and production.

I'm bullish on MitchRob because I don't consider Neemias Queta a threat to open as Boston's starting center. Robinson is one of the league's best rebounders, and his field-goal percentage and defensive contributions align with expectations for an elite fantasy center.

White will open the season as Charlotte's starting PG after LaMelo Ball was traded to Minnesota. Recent injuries to Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel could mean more work for White early on, giving him added fantasy upside.

The Rotoworld Staff reveals their biggest fades this season, including Jaylen Brown and Derik Queen.

▶ Name three players you're much lower on than the consensus.

Raphielle: G/F Austin Reaves (Los Angeles Lakers), F/C Alperen Şengün (Houston Rockets) and G/F Jaylen Brown (Philadelphia 76ers)

Reaves should be an excellent fantasy option this season, but I wonder if fantasy managers are underestimating the impact that LeBron's exit will have on the Lakers. Scoring opportunities won't be an issue for Reaves, but can he take on added playmaking responsibilities without his efficiency taking a hit? That's the question.

Şengün may be called "Baby Jokić" by some, but he has some deficiencies that hurt his fantasy value. The free-throw percentage is in "punt" territory, and turnovers can also be problematic. While the top-50 is a far expectation for Şengün, using a second-round pick on him is too much to pay.

Brown is well-positioned to contend for an NBA title in Philadelphia, but the trade did nothing for his fantasy outlook. LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey will handle a lot of the playmaking, and Joel Embiid will get his touches as well. Can Brown make up for the decreased usage with increased defensive numbers? Sure, but he isn't worth a third-round pick in standard drafts.

Noah: G/F Kon Knueppel (Charlotte Hornets), F Matas Buzelis (Chicago Bulls) and F/C Derik Queen (New Orleans Pelicans)

As mentioned previously, the hamstring injury will drop Knueppel's ADP, but I'm not interested in swinging for him. The Hornets seem to be building a team to shoot a ton of threes, which plays well for Knueppel. However, I'm concerned about how he looks without LaMelo Ball there. He's still really good and one of the league's best shooters, but I'm not confident he's ready to be a first or second option.

The blocks are nice, but I don't understand the appeal of taking Buzelis as early as he goes. He'll have to make a pretty substantial leap to return value at his ADP, and I don't foresee that happening. If you're a Buzelis believer, then I understand why you are banking on a breakout. But I don't see the path for it.

As mentioned previously, Queen will be good in the future, but I'm not interested in taking him before round 10. He has enough fantasy appeal to be worth selecting, but the situation in New Orleans is too messy for me to want a player who might not start.

Zak: C Jalen Duren (Detroit Pistons), F Paolo Banchero (Orlando Magic) and G Josh Giddey (Chicago Bulls)

Duren's contract situation has reportedly gotten ugly, and the $200 million man has new competition in John Collins, who can stretch the floor and also play some small-ball five. I'm not spending a third-round pick on him.

Banchero is another third-rounder I'm not high on for his lack of production in multiple categories. He doesn't shoot efficiently or hit threes at a high clip, and he doesn't rack up defensive stats.

Giddey had the best fantasy finish of his career last season, finishing 44th in eight-cat leagues. Can he really improve his fantasy stock with Norm Powell, Caleb Wilson and Nic Claxton now on the roster to steal usage and counting stats? His second-round asking price is far too rich for my blood.

▶ Which three players have the largest range of outcomes this season?

Raphielle: F/C Anthony Davis (Washington Wizards), G Kyrie Irving (Dallas Mavericks) and F Deni Avdija (Portland Trail Blazers)

Davis and Irving are returning after missing most (or all) of last season, and their situations have changed significantly. AD is on a roster that has Trae Young and a wealth of young talent, headlined by AJ Dybantsa. Also, can he stay healthy? Regarding Irving, he should lead the way alongside Cooper Flagg, but his availability has been an issue in recent years.

As for Avdija, his best season came before the Trail Blazers acquired Ja Morant, and Damian Lillard is back after missing the entire 2025-26 campaign. His usage is bound to decrease, which may not bode well for Deni's fantasy outlook.

Noah: G/F Brandon Miller (Charlotte Hornets), G Ja Morant (Portland Trail Blazers) and C Khaman Maluach (Phoenix Suns)

The Hornets have handed the keys to the franchise to Miller and Knueppel. Will they sink or swim? Miller has a bit more on-ball juice to me, and I could see him thriving as the new top option. However, he could also struggle in his new role and end up disappointing severely.

There's a scenario where Morant gets back to his former self on a new team with a new coach. More likely, he is limited in some capacity, which prevents that from happening. His injury history, regression when he's been on the floor in recent years, and competing with Damian Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson for minutes and touches, to name a few.

The stage is set for Maluach with Mark Williams set to miss an indefinite period of time. Maluach has the skill set to be a fantasy star, but will that happen this year? He could be ready and dominate the glass, swatting shots and even knocking down some deep-range shots. However, he didn't play much as a rookie, and he may not be ready, whereas Oso Ighodaro has much more experience.

Zak: G Tyrese Haliburton (Indiana Pacers), G Kyrie Irving (Dallas Mavericks) and F LeBron James (Philadelphia 76ers)

A perennial first-rounder in fantasy basketball, Haliburton missed all of last season after tearing his Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals. Will he return to form immediately, or will injuries and rust take their toll?

Too many question marks hang over Irving. Like Hali, he missed the 2025-26 season due to injury, but now he joins a new-look team that's building for the future rather than competing for a title. Can he stay on the court? What will be his role?

At this point in his career, LeBron can still make a serious impact on the court, but when does he fall off the inevitable cliff? Even if that doesn't happen this season, Philly has too many mouths to feed, and James' outlook has a wide array of potential outcomes.

The Rotoworld Basketball staff unveils their favorite draft picks this season, including Darius Garland and OG Anunoby.

▶ Name three late-round fliers you love taking.

Raphielle: G Cason Wallace (Oklahoma City Thunder), G/F Zach LaVine (Sacramento Kings) and F Yaxel Lendeborg (Golden State Warriors)

With the economics of today's NBA leading the Thunder to move Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins this summer, Wallace is in a great position in terms of playing time and fantasy outlook. He was a consistent starter when Oklahoma City was down a man last season; that should be his full-time role in 2026-27.

LaVine remains in Sacramento, and there's no reason to believe he won't start alongside Darius Acuff Jr. come Opening Night. Getting the veteran wing outside the top 100 would be a steal.

As for Lendeborg, he could begin the season as a starter. The first-round pick joins a team that won't have Jimmy Butler III or Moses Moody, as both continue to recover from knee injuries. Lendeborg's ability to facilitate offense makes him a good fit in the Warriors' scheme, and he's also solid defensively.

Noah: G Ajay Mitchell (Oklahoma City Thunder), G Darius Acuff Jr. (Sacramento Kings) and G/F Quentin Grimes (Los Angeles Lakers)

Sam Presti hyped Mitchell up during his preseason press conference, and there are multiple scenarios where he thrives this season. They traded Luguentz Dort this offseason to open a starting spot for Cason Wallace, which also means more minutes for Mitchell.

Talk about an upside swing here. Acuff will probably deal with some efficiency issues, as most rookie guards do. However, he was an offensive stud last season and could succeed as a rookie. Points, assists, and three-pointers will be his main contributions in year one, and if they want to make him the face of the franchise, he'll have the ball early and often.

I imagine Grimes will start, and while his role will mostly be off-ball, he has enough on-ball juice to pop. Grimes has a chance to be the No. 3 scoring option in Los Angeles, and with Luka Doncic facing double teams and dishing the ball around, he could thrive.

Zak: C Khaman Maluach (Phoenix Suns), G/F Keaton Wagler (LA Clippers) and F/C John Collins (Detroit Pistons)

Mark Williams is injured again, and Maluach will compete for the starting center gig in Phoenix. After an impressive Summer League showing, he could ride that momentum to a solid fantasy campaign.

The Clippers' roster is gutted, and Wagler should be running the show in the backcourt alongside Darius Garland. Garland and Brandon Ingram (who won't be available to start the season) are the only real threats to steal minutes from Wagler, so I expect him to see a ton of time and usage right out of the gate.

I have no faith in Jalen Duren's availability or motivation after an offseason filled with everything but basketball. Collins is a more effective scorer than Duren, and he can stretch the floor. The Pistons love surrounding Cade Cunningham with shooters, so the fit is obvious.

▶ Describe your favorite draft strategy.

Be flexible . Some managers can get so locked into getting their "guys" or what a ranking says about a player's value that they miss great opportunities to strengthen their teams. Being flexible in a draft can ultimately be the difference between winning your league and watching someone else take home the cash.

To use a basketball term, Read and React. It's really the only way to draft. Drafts are entirely unpredictable. If you do 80 mock drafts and then get to your real one, it may not go the way it did in practice. Pay attention to who everyone else is drafting. Don't go in thinking, "I'm going to get this player in round three." They might not be there. Read the draft room and other managers, and then react. - NR

BYOR: Bring your own rankings . I love comparing my personal rankings to the platform's default rankings pre-draft, but I love it even more to keep my rankings with me during the actual draft. With my rankings handy, I can draft appropriately, avoid reaching, identify values, and get "my guys" at the right time. Don't go into a draft with only a general idea of how you value players. Bring the rankings with you. - ZH

articles.title: The Heat could be good, the Hurricanes could be as well, and Jai Lucas says that's great for Miami
articles.summary: (AP) — Jai Lucas thinks the Miami Heat can help the Miami Hurricanes.The Hurricanes' coach — whose team was picked fourth in the Atlantic Coast Conference pr...
articles.body:
CORAL GABLES, Fla. (AP) — Jai Lucas thinks the Miami Heat can help the Miami Hurricanes.

The Hurricanes' coach — whose team was picked fourth in the Atlantic Coast Conference preseason poll — said Thursday that when the Heat are good, then it stands to reason that the entire area gets a little more fired up about basketball.

And after the acquisition of two-time NBA Most Valuable Player Giannis Antetokounmpo headlined a series of offseason moves that could make the Heat a contender again, Lucas expects excitement for basketball to be quite high in Miami.

"With Giannis being here and hopefully the success that the Heat has, I think it is all tied together," Lucas said at the Hurricanes' media day. "This is a pro city. It is a big metropolitan city. We're not in a small college town. So, everything is built on that and built on adding players that people want to come see and come watch in an entertaining environment. Absolutely, I think it's all tied together."

There are plenty of reasons why the Hurricanes should generate excitement on their own, after winning 26 games last season in Year 1 under Lucas and reaching the second round of the NCAA tournament. Miami opens this season Nov. 2 against Florida — a likely national title pick — in Tampa.

There is a history of the Hurricanes and Heat having strong seasons simultaneously. The Hurricanes' school record for wins in a season is 29, done twice — first in 2012-13 when the trio of LeBron James, Dwyane Wade and Chris Bosh were leading the Heat to an NBA title, then matched in the Hurricanes' Final Four season of 2022-23 when the Heat returned to the NBA Finals.

"I actually have seen it trickle down," Lucas said. "A lot of the recruits and a lot of people we're recruiting from Florida, these are the kids that are kind of the residual from when LeBron was here and growing up around that excitement with D-Wade and the Heat winning championships. That's their memory and that's how they started playing basketball. Now they're the kids you're recruiting and talking to them about it."

articles.title: Wemby Reveals New 'Standard' for Spurs Season After Becoming 'Best Defender on the Planet'
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama is already the "best defender on the planet," but the San Antonio Spurs star is raising the standard even higher going into the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama is already the "best defender on the planet," but the San Antonio Spurs star is raising the standard even higher going into the 2026-27 campaign.

"I've got a lot of growth to do," he told reporters . "I'm saying this because I have coaches that hold me to a very high standard. And now the standard isn't being the best on the planet anymore. It's being better than last year."

Wembanyama being even better is surely a terrifying idea for the rest of the NBA.

After all, his resume already includes a Defensive Player of the Year, three block titles, two All-Defensive nods, a Rookie of the Year, an All-NBA First Team selection and a Western Conference Finals MVP at 22 years old.

Being better than last year would be astounding, as he led the Spurs to the NBA Finals and took home that Defensive Player of the Year behind 3.1 blocks per game.

According to Basketball Reference , Wembanyama led the league in defensive rebound percentage (33.9), block percentage (9.4), defensive wins shares (5.0) and defensive box plus/minus (4.2), underscoring that his overall impact on that end of the floor goes well beyond just the number of shots he blocks.

What's more, there are all the shots that don't even happen, as his presence in the paint consistently discourages opponents from even driving the lane at all.

But at just 22 years old, it shouldn't be surprising Wembanyama is looking to improve. He has more experience in the league, fell just short of a championship and now seems in line to take another step.

It's just that the idea of the best defensive player in the world getting even better is surely a jarring one for offensive players.

articles.title: 'It's F--ked Up,' Carmelo Anthony Defends Angel Reese's 'Passion' Against Criticism
articles.summary: Ten-time NBA All-Star Carmelo Anthony came to the defense of Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese ahead of the 2026 WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
Ten-time NBA All-Star Carmelo Anthony came to the defense of Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese ahead of the 2026 WNBA Finals.

In the newest episode of his 7PM in Brooklyn show, a Wave original, Anthony argued some fans focus on Reese's swaggering personality and ignore her incredible body of work across all levels.

"The antics a lot of times overshadow that. But it's not antics, it's passion. It's her passion," he said (1:43:00 mark). "And when you come from where she comes from, you understand that passion. You understand that chip that you play with… And she shows that, she exudes that. And some people take that in a different way, but it's her passion. ...

Trade Ideas for Eliminated Playoff Teams💡

"Shout out to Angel. I just wanted to give her her flowers cuz that's beautiful and a lot of people won't give her flowers that way and it's unfortunate and it's f--ked up. But like let her live."

Reese became a household name during the 2023 NCAA tournament. Not only was she the Most Outstanding Player as LSU lifted a national title, but she unleashed some incredible taunts in the process.

After the triumph, Reese explained how it had a purpose.

"All year, I was critiqued for who I was. I don't fit the narrative," she said, per ESPN's Michael Voepel . "I don't fit the box that y'all want me to be in. I'm too hood. I'm too ghetto. Y'all told me that all year. When other people do it, and y'all don't say nothing.

"So this is for the girls that look like me. For those that want to speak up for what they believe in. It's unapologetically you. And that's what I [did] before tonight. It was bigger than me tonight. And Twitter is going to go into a rage every time."

The recently crowned Defensive Player of the Year hasn't changed since arriving in the WNBA. Now, she's adding the team success to go with her prolific rebounding and almost nightly double-doubles.

The Dream swept the Washington Mystics and New York Liberty to reach the Finals for the first time since 2013. Reese has averaged 18.0 points, 8.4 rebounds and 2.2 blocks during the postseason.

Getting this far is already an affirmation of the 6'4" forward's value. Should she lift a WNBA title, expect some raucous celebrations.

articles.title: Carmelo Anthony Reacts to Knicks Pausing Karl-Anthony Towns Contract Talks Ahead of New NBA Season
articles.summary: Carmelo Anthony reacted to the news that the New York Knicks were halting contract talks with Karl-Anthony Towns ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.
articles.body:
Carmelo Anthony reacted to the news that the New York Knicks were halting contract talks with Karl-Anthony Towns ahead of the 2026-27 NBA season.

"So, it was smart to dead the conversation," he said on his 7PM in Brooklyn podcast (1:22:23 mark). "Now, how you deaded the conversation is the problem. I can't find out on Twitter, if that's what happened."

When told that Towns said that the end of the talks were " news to me " and that he was "disappointed," Anthony continued.

GMs Pick MVP, ROY, More in Annual Survey 🗳️

"So if that's the case then that's a communication thing right there," he noted. "[The Knicks] dropped the ball on that one for one. You don't let that get outside. So again, I don't know that. The only thing I'm saying is you don't break up the family. That's all I'm going to say. You don't break up the family."

Towns, 30, is eligible for an extension worth up to $276 million but the Knicks reportedly have offered him a deal worth $200 million over four seasons as they attempt to avoid the second apron. With Towns clearly turning down that extension, the Knicks have ended the talks until after the season.

It's a bit of a gambit. Towns has a $61 million player option he could choose to turn down in the summer, becoming a free agent, although it would be a hefty chunk of change to turn down.

It's not exactly the storyline most New York fans would have preferred coming off the high of this summer's title. But for the time being, the band is back together, seeking a repeat.

articles.title: Angel Reese, A'ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart Headline 2026 WNBA All-Defensive Teams
articles.summary: The WNBA has announced its 2026 All-Defensive Teams:
articles.body:
The WNBA has announced its 2026 All-Defensive Teams:

Of note, Atlanta Dream forward/Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese and Las Vegas Aces center/five-time WNBA MVP A'ja Wilson are on the first team. New York Liberty forward and eight-time All-Star Breanna Stewart made the second team.

Trade Ideas for Eliminated Playoff Teams💡

This year marked Reese's first-ever All-Defensive team honor. She started 43 games for Atlanta after being traded from the Chicago Sky last offseason and helped the Dream finish second in defensive rating. Reese also amassed 7.3 defensive rebounds and 1.8 steals per game for Atlanta, which will face the Golden State Valkyries in the WNBA Finals. Reese's Dream teammate, guard Rhyne Howard, also made the first team. The four-time All-Star (in just five WNBA seasons) had 2.3 steals per game.

Wilson, this year's MVP and a three-time Defensive Player of the Year award winner, has made the All-Defensive first team each of the past five seasons. The nine-year pro had 1.9 blocks, 1.4 steals and 7.5 defensive boards per game. Wilson finished third in the DPOY race behind Reese and Golden State forward Gabby Williams.

Speaking of Williams, the two-time All-Star earned First Team honors for the second straight year. She is an incredible defensive presence, averaging 1.6 steals per game last season (and 1.6 SPG in her career). Williams played a huge role in Golden State's top-ranked defensive efficiency en route to the WNBA Finals.

Washington Wizards center Shakira Austin rounded out the first team. She finished second in the Most Improved Player race (behind Dallas Wings forward Jessica Shepard) in part because of her great defensive season. The Mystics ranked third in defensive efficiency, with Austin playing well.

On the second team, Stewart is now an eight-time All-Defensive team member after this year's honor.

Golden State guard Veronica Burton, last year's Most Improved Player, made the second team for the second straight season.

Dream guard Jordin Canada, a two-time All-Defensive First Teamer and two-time steals leader, also added 7.3 assists per game.

Washington Wizards guard Sonia Citron made her second All-Star team in as many seasons and has now added her first All-Defensive Team honor.

Golden State center Kiah Stokes made the All-Defensive Second Team in her first season (2015), and now she's done it again in year 11.

articles.title: 2026 WNBA Finals: The 7 questions that'll decide Dream-Valkyries
articles.summary: If you like physical defense, principled coaching, winning margins on the offensive glass, and put-a-bow-on-it storylines, this is the Finals matchup for you...
articles.body:
If you like physical defense, principled coaching, winning margins on the offensive glass and put-a-bow-on-it storylines, I have juuust the Finals matchup for you!

The Golden State Valkyries are set to face off against the Atlanta Dream in the 2026 WNBA Finals, which naturally means we're going to have a first-time champion. In fact, this is the first Finals series not to feature A'ja Wilson (Aces) or Breanna Stewart (Storm or Liberty) in five years, and only the second series without either of them in the last eight.

We're entering unfamiliar waters, folks.

A Valkyries win would be gratifying. Consider, among other things:

Gabby Williams, having a tremendous postseason run (22.7 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.0 assists, 1.8 steals), would win her first title in her first season with a new club.

Head coach Natalie Nakase would be a Year 2 champion, fresh off of leading the Valkyries to the playoffs in their inaugural season.

Kiah Stokes would add another ring to her collection, while Tiffany Hayes would earn her first.

It'd be one heck of a called shot from Joe Lacob, who gave the Valkyries a five-year timeline to win a championship. Five years for an expansion team is ambitious; winning it in the second year of existence? Whew .

A Dream win would also be gratifying. Consider, among other things:

Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray would earn their first titles together, further cementing them as one of the best wing duos in basketball.

Angel Reese would win her first WNBA title, months after being traded from the Chicago Sky.

DeWanna Bonner's departure from Phoenix would pay off, with her being a major contributor en route to her third ring.

Head coach Karl Smesko would be a Year 2 champion after making the leap from a storied college coaching career.

The storylines are awesome. These fanbases are energized — especially considering the recent news of the Dream being able to secure State Farm Arena for their upcoming home games. And, again, the basketball should be tantalizing.

On that front, we're going to take a look at some of the defining questions of this upcoming matchup.

Regular season: 108.2 ORTG (7th), 99.1 DRTG (1st), +9.1 net rating (1st)

Playoffs: 114.0 ORTG, 104.1 DRTG, +9.9 net rating

Regular season: 111.9 ORTG (4th), 103.5 DRTG (3rd), +8.4 net rating (3rd)

Playoffs: 113.2 ORTG, 102.0 DRTG, +11.2 net rating

July 4: Valkyries 88, Dream 83 (Isobel Borlase in the starting lineup for Atlanta, Naz Hillmon off the bench)

Whose perimeter defense will set the tone?

The Valkyries are headlined by Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton, first and second team All-Defense selections, respectively. Kayla Thornton can be tasked with guarding virtually anyone (more on that later), and Kaila Charles can hound you off the bench.

The Dream are headlined by Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada, also earning first and second team selections, respectively. Allisha Gray, if healthy (please be healthy), is a stout defender; DeWanna Bonner can still switch all over the place and bother folks with her length.

The Dream got a taste of strong perimeter defense in their first-round matchup with the Mystics, but the Valkyries haven't really dealt with a cast like this in the postseason. The Wings, ironically, didn't really have wings in the rotation — Awak Kuier was tasked with sliding up to deal with Williams, and Alysha Clark is more of a 4 that can slide up instead of a pure wing at this stage of her career. The Aces were notably light on that front, then had to navigate an absence and a minutes restriction from Steph Talbot on top of that.

Both of these perimeter groups are elite, even if they hit you at different times. The Valkyries are leading the postseason in backcourt pick-up rate (32.8%) and average pick-up distance (52.9 feet); the Dream are dead-last in both (3.2%, 34.5 feet).

I'm fascinated to see which cast of characters will be able to dictate terms and drag things into the mud.

We discussed this on the latest episode of "The Dunker Spot," but Reese has been especially good during the Dream's extended 10-game winning streak (last five of regular season, plus a 5-0 run during the playoffs so far). She's scoring more, scoring more efficiently, still being a menace on the glass, and her rim protection in particular has perked up — a scary development for this year's Defensive Player of the Year.

Through Aug. 29: 16.1 points (46.3% on 2s, 18% on 3s), 12.5 rebounds, 2.5 stocks, 65.1% FG allowed at the rim

During win streak: 18.2 points (53.7% on 2s, 35% on 3s), 8.9 rebounds, 3.3 stocks, 53.9% FG allowed at the rim

I'm especially fascinated by the finishing piece. The early growth she displayed in her attacks off the bounce — the early physicality paired with a quietly rising release point — started to pay off in the second half of the season.

It's been an up-and-down run so far in the postseason. She bounced back from a rough Game 1 against the Mystics (3-of-13 on 2s) to go a perfect 4-of-4 (plus three shooting fouls drawn) in Game 2. She went a combined 12-of-23 (52.2%) inside the arc in the first two games against the Liberty, before closing the series with a 5-of-14 (35.7%) clip in Game 3.

How will this look against a Kiah Stokes-led Valkyries group, especially following the series Stokes just had against reigning MVP A'ja Wilson?

To that end: Reese converted just 37.1% of her 2s against the Valkyries during their regular-season matchups, her second-lowest mark against any opponent (Mystics, 30.6%). If Reese is able to find more success this time around, it'd go a long way in helping to turn this series in Atlanta's favor.

Burton is coming off of a career-best campaign that, at minimum, has her in the conversation for an All-WNBA + All-Defense selection. Her ability to drive, playmake, knock down open shots (career-best 42.7% on catch-and-shoot 3s), and defend makes her one of the most impactful players in the league.

It's also fair to say it's been a bit of an odd postseason for her, particularly within the lens of scoring production. It'd be one thing if this was simply Burton missing shots; I'm more concerned — or maybe, amused? — by the shots she's turned down.

On a basic level, her shot attempts are down from the regular season (9.2 to 8.5). She's logged only one game of double-digit shot attempts (18 in Game 3 against Dallas). Her scoring efficiency is down this postseason: from 47.2% on 2s to 37.5%; from 35.5% on 3s to 31.6%.

And let's just say her approach (and effectiveness) as a driver were different when comparing the Wings and Aces matchups:

vs. Dallas: 20 direct drives, 1.0 PPP on direct drives, 65% shot attempt rate

vs. Las Vegas: 16 direct drives, 0.75 PPP on direct drives, 50% shot attempt rate

Burton did some of her best work against the Dream this season, with the Valkyries scoring an absurd 1.29 points per possession on trips featuring a Burton drive — the third-best mark against any opponent. I don't think the number will be that in this series, but the Valkyries certainly need her closer to that level compared to the Aces showing.

Is Rhyne Howard more prepared for the heat?

This is tied to the tone-setting defense point since Howard will likely be defended by Williams. It's worth broadening the scope in light of how the Valkyries treated her during the regular season.

Howard didn't have a good time, averaging just 13.3 points while shooting 25% from deep, in part because of how aggressive the Valkyries were against her. It's hard to establish a rhythm when you're consistently seeing bodies.

Not only did the Valkyries show help on 80% of Howard's drives, they blitzed her on over 32% of the ball screens she initiated. That was easily the highest clip of any of her opponents, and it makes sense that the Dream scored only 0.69 PPP on those trips.

Put another way: how much Janelle Salaün are we seeing in this series?

This year's unanimous Sixth Player of the Year has been pretty quiet this postseason — and seldom used. Her minute load has been nearly cut in half from the regular season (22.0 to 13.0); she hasn't logged double-digit minutes since Game 2 of the first round against Dallas.

The Valkyries turned to Aminata Gueye as a bulky, pain-inflicting reserve behind Stokes. Will they stick with that in preparation for whatever minutes Madina Okot logs for the Dream, or will they turn back to Salaün for her floor-spacing and self-creation?

What kind of cross-matching will we see?

A couple of things caught my eye in the last round on this front.

The Dream, like we saw in the regular-season matchups, gave Howard the Breanna Stewart assignment while Naz Hillmon defended Leonie Fiebich. On the other side of the country, the Valkyries often placed Thornton — and later, Cecilia Zandalasini — on Chelsea Gray while Burton operated as a roamer while "guarding" Bri Turner.

Will we get similar hijinks in the Finals?

Based on the regular-season matchups, the answer is a resounding "no." But these are the Finals; I wouldn't be surprised at all if the Valkyries sprinkled in some Thornton-on-Canada minutes, with Burton roaming off of Hillmon.

(It's worth noting the Dream, particularly in Game 2 against the Liberty, showcased a willingness to feed Hillmon — either on the block, or with quick-hitting actions — and poke at size mismatches.)

The Dream (35.5%) and Valkyries (32.2%) ranked first and fourth in offensive rebound rate during the regular season. That rate has risen for the Valkyries (35.7%) through two rounds, while it's dropped (28.9%) for the Dream — though their respective opponents certainly help explain that discrepancy.

Neither team could keep the other off the offensive glass during the regular-season meetings; the Dream grabbed 34.1% of their own misses, while the Valkyries grabbed 32.7% of theirs.

Also of note: the Valkyries were among the league's best in turnover suppression, only turning it over on 15.1% of their possessions this year (third-lowest). That number has dropped in the postseason (13.5%). The Dream were fine in that regard during the regular season (16.4%, sixth), but they've been spectacular at taking care of the ball during the playoffs (11.0%, first).

On the other end, the Dream famously turned teams over all year long — doing so at a league-leading 19.5% clip. That has somehow risen to 22.4% during the postseason; the Liberty are probably still trying to figure out what hit them. If you're reading this, you, too, have been ripped by Canada.

The Valkyries, meanwhile, were right behind the Dream in turnover-forcing (19.2%) during the regular season, though they haven't maintained that pace in the postseason (14.6%).

This is the more "boring" part of the series, but certainly among the most important. As basic as it sounds, the team that gets more shots up will likely win this series.

articles.title: Warriors rookie's reaction to learning he'd guard Lakers superstar Luka Dončić goes viral: 'What the f---?'
