articles.title: Angel Reese, A'ja Wilson headline WNBA All-Defensive first team
articles.summary: Angel Reese made her first ever All-Defensive team in 2026.
articles.body:
In her first season with the Atlanta Dream, Angel Reese took a significant leap forward. The 24-year-old showed out on the defensive side, winning her first Defensive Player of the Year award.

So it should come as no surprise that Reese was also named to the WNBA All-Defensive first team. Reese, alongside Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson, were among the biggest names to make the first team, the league announced Thursday.

Reese was joined by her teammate Rhyne Howard on the squad. Shakira Austin of the Washington Mystics and Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries were the other team players to receive first team honors.

The Dream were also represented on the second team, where Jordin Canada landed. Two members of the Valkyries, Veronica Burton and Kiah Stokes, made it as well, with Mystics guard Sonia Citron and New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart rounding out the list.

Other than Reese, the only other player on either team to win the Defensive Player of the Year award in their career is Wilson, who's taken home that award three times. For Wilson, Thursday's selection marks the sixth time she's made the WNBA All-Defensive team and the fifth time she's been selected to the first team.

For Reese, it marks the first time in her career she's been picked to be on the WNBA All-Defensive team.

After making the first team last season, Williams went back-to-back with that honor in 2026. She also has a second-team selection from 2022. Howard's selection marks the first time she made the first team. She was a second-team selection last season. For Austin, it marks the first time in her career she's been selected for the WNBA All-Defensive team.

On the second team, Burton, Canada, Stewart and Stokes all have previous WNBA All-Defensive selections. Citron is a new addition to the WNBA All-Defensive team. After falling short of the honor during her rookie season, Citron made the second team in Year 2.

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey Says Healthy Joel Embiid 'Changes Everything' as 76ers Prep for Debut with LeBron James
articles.summary: For the first time in years, Joel Embiid is entering the NBA season healthy.
articles.body:
For the first time in years, Joel Embiid is entering the NBA season healthy.

Tyrese Maxey said that having Embiid healthy "changes everything" as the team prepares for its first season with LeBron James.

"You can put in more packages," Maxey said, per ESPN's Kris Rhim . "There's been times where he hasn't been healthy and we get into the game and now we're trying to learn on the flow."

Since his MVP campaign in 2022-23, Embiid hasn't played more than 39 games in a season while dealing with various injuries, mainly a knee ailment. That has caused him to miss key parts of the offseason, like training camp.

"If you haven't been playing with a big like Joel, there's not many. It's very hard, very difficult to learn certain things," he said. "...So, with him being here, we can drill those things over and over. It's been what, like two, three weeks that we've had just drilling and drilling. That's a good thing."

When healthy, Embiid is one of the best players in the league, but it has been a while since fans have seen that version of him. This year, it could be a different story.

While he's entering the season healthy, Philadelphia will surely be cautious with Embiid throughout the regular season. The Sixers need him, James and Maxey at their best when the playoffs roll around, and they'll need to manage their stars' minutes wisely to avoid any setbacks.

articles.title: Valkyries GM's strategy once shocked WNBA world. Now it's in awe of her Finals squad
articles.summary: Skepticism and doubt were two common reactions to how general manager Ohemaa Nyanin assembled the Golden State Valkyries roster. It turns out she built a WNB...
articles.body:
Those were two reactions the outside world had about the way the new Golden State Valkyries were constructing their roster. Through one expansion draft, two collegiate drafts and two trade deadlines, outsiders couldn't quite get a handle on Ohemaa Nyanin 's strategy.

Was the focus of the franchise other team's cast offs? Did they not want collegiate stars? Were they allergic to star power?

It turns out that what general manager Nyanin was doing, with intentionality and care, was constructing a team that would compete for a championship in just its second year of existence.

She was looking for specific characteristics. For two-way players, for defensive buy-in, for high-character people, for athletes who were versatile and team-oriented. Women who would also be ambassadors for the new franchise and part of the community.

"Relentless pursuit of excellence is a big thing," Nyanin said Thursday on a conference call, two days before the Valkyries host the Atlanta Dream in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals. "Not allowing for 'no' to be the end of your story. Really trying to find ways to problem solve and pivot.

"Wanting to buy into a system and really wanting to be connected, not just on the court but off the court."

That last point is key to Nyanin's approach. She has created a connected team in every sense of the word. The players talk about their chemistry, their bond, their joy of playing with and for each other.

And much of that begins with how the woman at the top of basketball operations treats them.

Golden State Valkyries vs. Atlanta Dream Best of seven series:

Oct. 17: 12:30 p.m. at Chase Center; NBC Oct. 19: 5 p.m. at Chase Center; USA, CNBC Oct. 21: 5 p.m. in Atlanta; USA, CNBC Oct. 24: 10 a.m. in Atlanta; NBC Oct. 26*: 5 p.m. at Chase Center; USA, CNBC Oct. 29*: 5 p.m. in Atlanta; USA, CNBC Oct. 31*: 5 p.m. at Chase Center; USA, CNBC

Gabby Williams has known Nyanin for a long time, through international basketball connections and Nyanin's days as the assistant general manager of the New York Liberty, where Williams' partner Marine Johannes plays.

"It's been great watching her grow into a leadership role," Williams said. "Something that's never wavered is her attention to detail, the pride she takes in doing things the right way and the pride she takes in getting to know players and making sure they're taken care of.

"Going after great people, not just great basketball players. I think working closely with players for a long time allowed her to understand the importance of that. She was always a players' relations person. Even when I would go visit Marine in New York, she would make sure I was taken care of."

Nyanin is a nurturing presence. She helps Williams find a cat sitter. She reminds Natalie Nakase to eat. She wants to make sure her people have whatever they need to do their jobs without worry.

"She just lets me coach," Nakase said. "So I don't have to worry about so much. … Her care factor for every second that we're breathing is just unmatched. When you feel like you're cared for and loved, you feel like you could be your best. She's the mom of all of us, constantly thinking about what else could she do? She wants to improve.

"Leaders are great because they care about people, not about themselves. And I think Ohemaa thrives in that role."

Nyanin originally put together a team with overlooked or discarded gems, players who had been made expendable by other teams. They added little from their first collegiate draft: Justė Joyctė who stayed in Europe, Shyanne Sellers who was waived before the season, and Kaitlyn Chen , a third-round pick with little expectation. The result was a historic playoff berth in the team's first year.

There was more opportunity in the second year. A massive free-agent market with a new collective bargaining agreement. A talent-rich collegiate draft. But, again, Nyanin was intentional and unwavering in her vision.

Knowing how much upheaval and movement the new CBA would bring to many teams, she opted for continuity with much the same roster that had achieved so much, so early. She added a stellar two-way player in Williams that she had been watching for years, who has blossomed into a league star, and Kiah Stokes, a lynchpin center with three championship rings. She re-signed or extended the core of the team.

On draft night, when the team drafted Flau'jae Johnson eighth overall and then immediately traded her to Seattle, it shocked the WNBA world. The trade, Nyanin later said, had been agreed upon ahead of time. The overall takeaway was that the Valkyries were happy with what they had. Nyanin thought they could go a long way with the roster they had constructed.

The one thing that surprised Nyanin was how quickly the team came together this season, merging the core players and the newcomers.

"You never know how it's going to work out," she said. "The athletes did as much work as myself and the staff in trying to get to know one another on a deeper level. … The amount of time they put in with each other on and off the court."

"Ohemaa should not be ignored for the force that she is in sports," said team president Jess Smith. "How she has constructed these rosters, how she has hired, how she has built a culture in two years - it's something organizations have tried to do for decades."

Nyanin's boss is a man who likes stars, who signed Kevin Durant and has pursued LeBron James. But Nyanin said it didn't take a lot to convince team owner Joe Lacob to buy into her vision and plan of a team-oriented group, light on big-name stars and super heavy on character.

"What he has done is empower us as leaders to really lead with our heart and with our strategy and experiences," Nyanin said. "He's done an amazing job of balancing asking questions and being inquisitive and sharing his past experiences to help us create the team we have today."

Nyanin has had a vision. It has come together quickly. The moment she realized it had manifested in reality was when the players huddled on court, down double digits, in an elimination game against Dallas and took a breath together.

"The collective moment of breath was the epitome of things we have said here and there," Nyanin said. "All the little things we've put together. A breath to say, they will fight with each other and for each other.

"And that's exactly why I'm doing the job that I'm doing."

articles.title: NBA Vegas preseason power rankings: Thunder ranked No. 1, ahead of Victor Wembanyama's Spurs
articles.summary: Our NBA handicapper gives his preseason power rating for all 30 NBA teams.
articles.body:
Prior to the NFL season, I published an article on the preseason NFL power ranking for all 32 teams on Yahoo Sports. In that article, I explained how to use a ratings system to help price spreads, how to use it to action bets and what potential pitfalls in the process exist. I highly recommend reading that article to also lay the foundation for my NBA power ratings below.

Instead of retooling the same concepts into NBA terms, I am going to provide my ratings and then note which teams I see as potential risers and fallers once the NBA regular season action begins. These are currently built off of using NBA regular season win totals, title odds to differentiate teams with the same win total number, current state of injury news, and the first few regular season games we have priced. I then add some manual adjustment. The only major difference to note in using these instead of NFL is the change in home-court rating from 1.5 to 3 points from a neutral site.

Here are my NBA preseason power ratings for all 30 NBA teams.

The Rockets were second in overall market rating last season prior to Steven Adams getting injured and missing the rest of the season. At the time, they were the No. 1 rebounding team, and the NBA's best in 3-point shooting team. The latter might be surprising, but these concepts relate: Forcing opposing teams to crash the glass leaves perimeter shooters wide open for second chance points in catch and shoot threes with high shot quality. Not only do they Rockets get Adams back, but also Fred VanVleet and they added Marcus Smart. They are a no-brainer over 47.5 on the win total, a sneaky division winner long shot, and might be dangerous in the playoffs if they can stay healthy.

The trendiest offseason pick is the Jazz to surpass 36.5 regular season wins, and I don't disagree. This is like fantasy football preseason Parker Washington buzz, and it instantly paying off. Utah is loaded with young talent and has an elite coach in Will Hardy who can put it all together. They have been waiting to step up into real competition for a few years, focused on rebuilding (and tanking), and now they can hit the gas pedal. I wouldn't be surprised if they are the biggest riser this year and in short order being a top-10 team that doesn't look back.

This is the hardest team to figure out. A new head coach, Kyrie Irving coming back, Derrick Lively still hurt but getting healthier and Cooper Flagg — who might be an All-Star starter and All-NBA player, or might need another year of development. In full transparency, I took Flagg to win most improved player at 100-1 odds and the win total under 34.5, so am I flummoxed which way this goes. But Dallas the tools to quickly rise. If Flagg completely pops, if Irving and Lively are healthy and if coach Dusty May is an upgrade from Jason Kidd, I wouldn't be surprised if they are league average and locked into a play-in bid. Right now, they are marketably below average.

The lifting Nikola Jokic has to do exceeds any other player in the NBA by a mile. The potential problem is if Jokic's efficiency drops like it did last season at the midway point and into the playoffs. Both Jokic's 3-point percentage and finishing around the rim fell off, and his defense remains a problem. Aaron Gordon lost a step athletically, so did Jamal Murray and Peyton Watson is no longer on the team. Less depth and waning star power could cause a drop off.

Last season, this team thrived by putting intense pressure on the ball, moving in transition and generating free throws. This year the league-mandated referee initiatives to call more offensive fouls on illegal screens and push offs could hurt Portland more than other teams. They also lost their coach, some of the back-of-house staff and a few players that fit very well, like Matisse Thybulle.

They added Ja Morant and return Damian Lillard, who are good additions but don't fit the way they play. I don't view new head coach Micah Nori that highly, and he may struggle to put it all together cohesively.

There is one team actually incentivized to tank this season, and it's the Nets. They owe the Houston Rockets their first-round pick and if it lands No. 1, they lose the right to draft No. 1 the following year even without keep the pick this year. Therefore, it might make sense to finish bottom three in the "relegation zone", where they reduce the chance of landing the first pick. For that reason, they may play worse lineup combinations, they may trade Michael Porter Jr or Julius Randle and they may be a lone team that gets significantly worse this season (although they are saying otherwise publicly at the moment).

articles.title: A’ja Wilson adds one more accolade to wrap up 2026
articles.summary: While the championship case will not see a new addition this year, A’ja Wilson still has some individual achievements to mark the 2026 season.
articles.body:
While the championship case will not see a new addition this year, A'ja Wilson still has some individual achievements to mark the 2026 season.

On Thursday, the five-time MVP and Las Vegas Aces superstar was named to the 2026 All-Defensive First Team.

This is the fifth straight season where Wilson has been named to the first team, as well as her sixth year on the All-Defensive team (she was named to the second team in 2020).

Joining Wilson are the Atlanta Dream's Angel Reese and Rhyne Howard, the Golden State Valkyries' Gabby Williams and the Washington Mystics' Shakira Austin.

Wilson earned her spot in the lineup by leading the league in blocks for the fifth consecutive year, averaging an impressive 1.9 rejections per game. She also lead the league with 3.3 stocks (steals + blocks per game, while also finishing in the top five in defensive rebounds (third with 7.5 rpg), total rebounds (9.4 rpg, fifth) and defensive win shares (3.1, fourth).

The 2026 season also saw Wilson reach some defensive career milestones.

On Aug. 3 against Atlanta, Wilson officially moved ahead of Hall of Famer Lauren Jackson for sixth all-time in total blocks, finishing the season with 612 for her career. She also recorded her 1,000th stock to become the 10th player in WNBA history to reach that mark.

While Wilson is now contending with Reese for the best defensive player in the WNBA, the three-time Defensive Player of the Year has shown that she can still be reliable in protecting the basket.

articles.title: Vanessa Richardson leaves Rockets’ broadcast role for full-time ESPN position
articles.summary: Space City Home Network (SCHN) will have a new courtside reporter for its Rockets broadcasts after losing Vanessa Richardson to a full-time gig at ESPN.
articles.body:
NBA reporter Vanessa Richardson is leaving her post as courtside reporter with the Houston Rockets to take a national position with ESPN.

Richardson had previously worked with ESPN on a contract basis, and she's now turning that into a full-time role.

In Houston, Richardson was employed by Space City Home Network (SCHN) — the regional sports network owned in part by the Rockets — since the start of the 2022-23 season.

Richardson, who won multiple Lone Star Emmy awards for her coverage of the team, announced the news on her social media accounts. As part of an extended message, she wrote:

Serving as sideline reporter of the Rockets for the past four seasons did not just change my career, it changed my life. … A few years ago, I began working part-time at ESPN as a fill-in sports talk radio host. Each opportunity for growth has been a dream; from digital shows at the NBA Finals to reporting at summer league, the draft, and every event with this league I love so much. I'm grateful to continue to the journey at ESPN in an expanded role, and I'm ready to get to work. I've loved every second of the past four years. Thank you to everyone who has been a part of it.

articles.title: El 'Tigre' vuelve a rugir: Andrés Feliz revienta al ASVEL con ocho triples
articles.standfirst: El dominicano lidera el triunfo del Real Madrid con 26 puntos (8/11 triples), 4 rebotes, 5 asistencias en 25 minutos
articles.summary: El dominicano lidera el triunfo del Real Madrid con 26 puntos (8/11 triples), 4 rebotes, 5 asistencias en 25 minutos
articles.body: El martes Andrés Feliz lideró el triunfo del Real Madrid en Milán con su mejor partido en la Euroliga y ante el ASVEL Villeurbane el 'Tigre' de Guachupita volvió a demostrar su voracidad con otra actuación colosal que terminó quebrando la resistencia gala (111-92). El dominicano acabó con 26 puntos (8/11 triples), cuatro asistencias y cinco rebotes en apenas 25 minutos para un total de 30 créditos de valoración, su nuevo récord. Difícil hacer más en menos tiempo. No estuvo solo Feliz, que tuvo en Maledon, otro que está de dulce (16+5+9 y 6 faltas recibidas) a su mejor socio. El ASVEL compareció sin tres de sus mejores jugadores (Patty Mills, Joe Crowder y Tremont Waters), pero salió a jugar sin complejos, a mil por hora y con tiros rápidos de Washington (17), Besson (16), Jackson (13+6 asistencias) y Bolomboy (12+7). Pero ese modus operandi no le fue mal al Madrid, que en el intercambio de golpes suele llevar las de ganar. Los blancos aceptaron la apuesta y la subieron de inicio con los triples de Procida, Feliz, Jones y Pradilla para contrarrestar los del inspirado Sestina (25-17, min 58). Jackson y Cale se sumaron a ese festival del triple para acercar a su equipo (27-25, min 10). Mucho acierto de ambos y poquita defensa. Esa dinámica se mantuvo al inicio del segundo acto, con triples de Jackson, Smit Jr. y Procida en un intercambio de golpes que mantuvo la igualdad en el marcador (35-34) hasta que Maledon se adueñó del balón para liderar un 8-1 (43-35, min 15). El francés se sentó y saltaron a cancha Feliz y Campazzo para tomar su testigo, especialmente el dominicano, que con dos triples y ocho puntos comandó un parcial de 13-3 (56-41, min 19). El acierto de Washington evitó que los blancos hiciesen más sangre antes del descanso (61-48). En la reanudación un Luwawu-Cabarrot negado en este inicio de campaña puso la máxima con un triple (64-48). Pero Besson y Bolomboy reactivaron a los galos con un 0-9 (64-57). Pedro Martínez buscó la fórmula del éxito juntando a Maledon con Feliz, y el quinto triple del 'Tigre' de Guachupita dio aire a los suyos (68-57, min 24). No cejó en su empeño el ASVEL, que empató con los triples de Jackson y Cale y un 2+1 de Dada (71-71). La inspiración del Madrid se esfumó en el tercer acto (3/13 triples), pero tomaron aire con cuatro puntos de Maledon y un palmeo sobre la bocina de Pradilla (77-71, min 30). Feliz aún no había saciado su hambre y lideró un parcial de 14-4 con dos triples, a los que se sumaron los de Okeke y Abalde para dejar encarrilado el triunfo (100-86, min 37). Los galos ya no tuvieron fuerzas, ni acierto ni fe para intentar remontar. Abalde y Maledon echaron el cierre al partido que acabó con la máxima diferencia blanca (111-92). 111 – Real Madrid (27+34+16+34): Feliz (26), Maledon (16), Procida (8), Okeke (10), Tavares (9) -cinco inicial-, Smith Jr. (7), Campazzo (3), Pradilla (12), Jantunen (6), Luwawu-Cabarrot (3), Abalde (6) y Jones (5). 92 – LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne (25+23+23+21): Fodzo Dada (6), Besson (16), Sestina (8), Gach (6), Pons (2) -cinco inicial-; Cale (8), Washington Jr. (17), Massa (4), Jackson (13), Bolomboy (12), Lighty (-). Árbitros: Milivoje Jovcic (Serbia), Seffi Shemmesh (Israel) y Eduard Udyanskyy (Reino Unido). Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido de la sexta jornada de la Euroliga disputado en el Movistar Arena de Madrid ante 6.723 espectadores.
